;御神書

;中野與之助

English explanation: These are excerpts from works by Yonosuke Nakano, the founder of Ananaikyo (三五教), a Japanese new religion derived from Oomoto and Honda Chikaatsu's philosophy.

==The Universe as Observed from the Spirit World==
===1===
:1
:From ''The Universe as Observed from the Spirit World'', Vol. 5: "Celestial Phenomena" ①
:(Published February 1966)
:"God is a Mirror"

:When observed from the spirit world, the forms of people at work on earth are reflected in the spirit world as in a mirror, revealing all aspects of that person's mind. In the spirit world, both falsehood and truth are reflected. When something appears in the spirit world, it manifests in the present world — and this is why the present world is called the "manifested world" (genzei). To take God as a mirror is what this means. Humanity, born by divine command, is a divided spirit and divided body of God, and from birth is bestowed with a soul from God. For this reason humanity is called "the lord of all creation" (banbutsu no reichō). This lordship becomes the soul of the universe. It is good to fulfill our mission based on the great spirit of the universe. Human life has meaning only in accordance with God's great divine will.

===2===
:2
:From ''The Universe as Observed from the Spirit World'', Vol. 7: "Spirit, God, and Humanity" ②
:(Published April 1966)
:"The Soul is the Progenitor of Humanity"

:Humans possess both spirit (rei) and soul (tamashii). The soul is naturally bestowed upon each individual from birth as a heaven-given gift. There is not a single person without a soul. Without a soul, one is the same as a corpse. The spirit is the spirit of divine essence. When an individual's soul is united in harmony with the divine spirit of the universe, this is called reikon (spirit-soul) — that is, the union of humanity and God. To be clearly spiritual, one must commune with the divine spirit of the great universal spirit, hold the confidence that "I am divine," and become fully divine. Without spirit there is neither mind nor God; without soul there is no body. Since the spirit-soul is the progenitor of humanity, it is of utmost importance. It is bestowed upon us from God's divine mind as divided spirit. That which teaches such things is called religion. It is good for humanity to know the ancestral God who is the giver of the spirit-soul. It is through understanding the spirit-soul that one knows the God who is the source of the universe. Knowing the living great spirit of the universe is humanity knowing itself. When one knows the spirit-soul, one knows the source of the spirit of the universe — and this is called knowing human life. Let us describe one aspect of the workings of the soul bestowed by God at birth. A newborn infant who cannot yet see, and who has no discernment, demands milk and cries out when it touches something hot. Such self-protection is the work of the soul, which acts to seek the satisfaction of the individual.

===3===
:3
:From ''The Universe as Observed from the Spirit World'', Vol. 9: "Spiritual Industry and Industrial Spirit"
:(Published September 1966)
:"The Way of Life"

:The word "life" (seimei) is written with characters meaning "the command to live" — but exactly who gives this command? The origin of the life of all humanity and creation is the great life-force, and one must know that humanity and all creation were brought forth as products of cosmic industry along the path of great life, in accordance with the commands of the cosmic will which governs and presides over all the phenomena of the universe.

:Just as one's own image is reflected in a mirror, just as a person gives birth to a child resembling themselves, humanity reflects the cosmos and lives with a body that is a microcosm of the universe. The human body is constructed according to the truth of the universe. Even in the matter of birth, although there may be physical parents, life cannot be created and produced by human power alone. The power of cosmic creation sets the processes of nature in motion within the mother's womb, giving the embryo the power to develop. After being born from the mother's body into the world, one is connected directly to the great life-force and great spirit, and guarded along the way of life. Protected by the profound virtue of heaven and earth from birth, one grows through the nurturing of the great sky; and by receiving the spiritual education of heaven, earth, and the universe before physical education, one's lifeline gradually grows strong, bound to the great life-force, and one comes to walk the righteous path.

===3-1===
:3-1
:From ''The Great Way of World Salvation'' ①
:(Published December 1965)
:"The True Significance of Humanity"

:When one consults a dictionary to interpret what a human being is, one finds: "The most evolved and superior being among animals; the being endowed with the faculties of language, thought, and reason." This is a merely physical and academic interpretation. Interpreted spiritually, since humanity originates in the cosmic will and is born of the ancestral God, it is important first to understand the great spirit of the ancestral God and to deeply understand the significance of humanity. Though heaven and earth conceive all creatures and creation, within the invisible, atmospheric, transparent body there are natural vital essences, and by the ancestral God's divine will — that is, by the cosmic will — the life of all creation on earth takes root. The work of the ancestral God in creating within the great void is spiritual industry; when born physically and materially on earth, it is called industrial spirit. Within the invisible, atmospheric, transparent body there are the life-nurturing essences of all creation, and spiritual industry is carried out — but even if one wishes to explain and convey this interpretation to people, there are no words with which to explain it. I believe that as people's minds advance further, words will naturally be born. For now, those who are conceived within the cosmos and born on earth are interpreted as humanity. Since all of humanity and creation were born through the power of great nature, it is most correct to interpret this spiritually. Physically, human beings are born and raised by their human parents; but spiritually, one must not forget the existence of the ancestral God of the universe, who invisibly and in the shadows bestows life, sends air and vital breath, and gives the power to live.

===4===
:4
:From ''The Universe as Observed from the Spirit World'', Vol. 7: "Spirit, God, and Humanity" ③
:(Published May 1966)
:"Without Religion, Nothing Exists"

:The world of divine spirits is called the great spirit realm. The working of the spiritual power of the great natural universe is called God. The working of the natural spiritual power that governs the universe has no name and is difficult to name. The human realm and the natural realm differ. When one observes a person from the spirit world, divine spirit-elements are interlaced in a net-like, crossing pattern, constituting a single person. Through some degree of spiritual practice — transcending knowledge, setting aside one's own will, proceeding into the spirit world spiritually and purely in accordance with God's divine will — one can only be astonished at the sight: ten-thousand fine spirit-lines working in the yin-yang arrangement, interwoven like a net, all gathering into a single unified form. It is the work of God that the divine spirit-elements of the universe act to give power to all creation and govern life. If one gazes upon the great spirit of all things in heaven and earth from the spirit world, it is so vast and grand that it is impossible to describe. The simplest thing for all people is to accept as-is what a person of spiritual wisdom and spiritual awakening sees in the spirit world and expounds. Gazing upon the spirit world, one comes to know great things. Spiritually communing with the divine will, one comes to regard the universe as one's own home and to develop the great magnanimity of living together with God — and through this, one draws out teachings on all matters from God's great spirit and conveys God's divine will to the world. By mastering the spirit world, one reaches God's great spirit. One comes to know that humanity is operated by God. Living based on God's great spirit, it becomes clear that one dwells in the house called the universe. Teaching the cosmic will through great education, calming the spirit within people, and acting based on God's divine will is the manifestation of God's will. To venture an opinion about the spirit world without knowing it is to commit a spiritual sin. It is important to savor this truth well. Everything is summed up in the single phrase: "Without religion, nothing exists."

===5===
:5
:From ''The Universe as Observed from the Spirit World'', Vol. 7: "Spirit, God, and Humanity" ⑤
:(Published May 1966)
:"Reikon and Yūkon"

:A person has a body, and the mind — that is, spirit — communicates with God; one has the nature to receive enough spiritual power to become one with mind and God. For this reason, when one is granted spiritual power, one becomes greatly active. Death is merely the passing of the body; that person's spirit-soul (more properly called yūkon, shadow-soul) is imperishable. Within the spirit are the four souls — ara (rough), nigi (harmonious), sachi (fortunate), and kushi (wondrous). When all four souls are complete, this is called spirit. The workings of the four souls are the workings of the spirit. What one masters in one's mind through those workings is called spirit. From birth, a person is endowed with a soul as a heaven-given gift to protect the body; but as the mind advances spiritually, one summons the spirit, and within the heart the yin-yang of spirit and soul unite and act as one.

:The spirit belongs entirely to the cosmic spirit realm, and it is not possible for a human being to become entirely cosmic spirit. A person with a body belongs wholly to the bodily world and cannot become entirely spirit. In truth, it is not possible to truly embody the spirit within oneself and perfectly complete the spirit-soul — but the word "reikon" (spirit-soul) is so commonly and naturally used in the present world that confusion easily arises. It is important to know the true dignity of spirit. It is more correct to call reikon "yūkon" (shadow-soul).

:When the yūkon departs the physical body, it goes to the other world. To go to the other world is to go to the divine world. Both the spirit realm and the shadow realm are worlds created by God, and are therefore called the divine world. God created humanity on earth, and after death one continues to act as a yūkon. When departing for the shadow realm after death, the soul is a spiritual body invisible to the human eye. When the spirit unites with that spiritual body through practice, this is called reikon. The path of practice from yūkon to reikon is not easy; through purification by the teachings of the great life-force, passing through the shadow realm and the middle shadow realm and reaching the spirit — this is the most noble and most exalted path of practice.

==The Joy of Human Completion==
;The Joy of Human Completion

===1===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt 1

From "The Joy of Human Completion"

The great spirit of the universe is what is called God.

God is without form, without voice, a divine working invisible to human eyes. God's life works both spiritually and physically. God, with vigorous and vibrant energy, organizes the workings of the natural universe and carries on cosmic life. All people and all creatures are constituted by the power of creation and nurturing of the cosmic great ancestral God (Mioya). Furthermore, all creation grows by the power of creation and nurturing; depending on the thing — grains ripen and grow with power renewed each year — human life becomes possible, and God is active along the path by which all things flourish. The life of the universe is the cyclic, orderly rhythm of the cosmos, what one may also call the cosmic great life-force, the working of God. God's working gives its power without exception to all creation, and does not cease for even a moment. This is what people call the power of nature. Day by day the world is organized by natural power, giving life to things, working and nurturing them as they transform — this is what is called life. The life of the universe is truly organized by the astonishing power of God. The celestial bodies — sun, moon, and stars — are active with the spirit of one great family. The entire universe is God, and in the great void there is the mysterious divine activity of God invisible to human eyes. The celestial realm is yin. The earth, in contrast, is body and yang. We are divided spirits of the cosmic God. We are children of the cosmic God and shrines of God — hence the term "microcosm of the universe." Humanity cannot exist in this world even for a moment apart from the spirit of the cosmic God. If the people of the universe were to depart this world in vain, then heaven too would depart in vain, the great earth too would depart in vain, and the great way too would depart in vain. The universe and humanity are existences that absolutely cannot be separated. Moreover, if the universe and humanity were separated, people would pass away in vain. The universe and humanity are one.

(To be continued)

===2===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt 2

(Continued from last time)

Because people look up at the sky and give it the name "sky," there is sky; because they look at the earth and call it "great earth," there is earth; because they look at all creation and call it "all creation," there is all creation; because they say "yin and yang," there is yin and yang. Because people have given these names, and because people believe that what is named exists, there are heaven and earth, yin and yang, and all creation. If humanity ceased to exist, all words too would cease. Whether or not things exist, when the names of things cease, their forms too disappear. For this reason, if humanity were to disappear, all things too would entirely disappear — the same principle as the roots withering when a tree or grass loses its leaves. The completion of humanity and the completion of the universe together constitute the flourishing of cosmic humanity. Even a single tree, a single blade of grass, receives nourishment from its roots by the light of sun and moon and the power of the earth — that is, the power of heaven and earth — absorbs vital essence through its leaves, and grows. One cannot see the nurturing power given to things that causes them to be born, grow, and develop. This is what is meant by "spiritual." It is in what is invisible, what is not a thing, that God's working exists. The blowing of the wind, the falling of rain — these are not human handiwork. It is all by God's providential care that creation is generated, grows, and develops.

The physical is only what the eyes can see, only what the ears can hear, only what individual knowledge can perceive — this is what is called physical. Even what one thinks of as spiritual, if it is conceived in the mind of individual knowledge, is physical spirit or intellectual spirit — small spirit in comparison with God's great spirit.

Humanity must take the spiritual as its foundation; spiritual life based on the spiritual must be the basis of everything. That life is the bond between God's great spirit and humanity's small spirit. Acting in spiritual life under the cosmic great spirit, if the spirit is renewed by the power of creation and nurturing, then naturally all the organization of the universe, all cosmic life, can be perceived by human spirit. For this reason, humanity must return to the image of the cosmic God, cultivate spiritual magnanimity, build conviction, gain self-awareness, and open the path of communion with God. Through the study of spirit, one comes to know the divine realm. Mastering the mysteries of the great void is precisely coming to know the spirit world. This lies in transferring the activity of the great nature of the universe to human spirit and living in accordance with the great spirit of the cosmos. In that life, light, power, and virtue arise.

From the great spirit — that is, the cosmic will — a derived will is issued; the cosmic will and human will are joined, and a spiritual and physical bond is formed, creating for people a world of will. Spiritually and physically inheriting the cycle, orderly rhythm, and order of the universe, the path of advancing rightly is called human life. Both the cosmos and humanity live to protect life. For this reason, religious persons, in guiding along the way of life, guide by the cosmic great spirit. We are born into this world, and it is important to master the high virtue of the cosmic ancestral God (Mioya). Since humanity is born with a spiritual nature — spirit is divine, and we must receive and carry on the great spirit of God and be active. Human life is devoted to seeking the advancement of spirit and the advancement of the material world, working with ten-thousand transformations according to the law of cosmic truth, renewing superstition and false belief and returning to the direction of goodness. If one opens the state of union of God and humanity — divine-human oneness — one can draw everything, all of it, into one's spirit. And then a person becomes one soul of the universe — each a distributed portion from God — becoming the soul of the physical body. Heaven-deity and earth-person must be one. The way is to live under the organization of the universe. Taking the spiritual and physical as one, inheriting the cosmic will, one must advance on the path of human completion.

(To be continued)

===3===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt 3

(Continued from last time)

Spiritually and physically, one must not kill a single thing but must give life to all creation. The meaning of "do not kill a single thing" is not that one must not catch fish or slaughter cattle and pigs for food. Having obtained nutrition, to make full use of it and cause that energy to act for the purposes of God — that is making full use of it, and humanity acts as proxy for the mission of all creation. To give life means to live according to that mission. Through this, a person's spirit lives without opposing God's divine will and without going against the cosmic atmosphere. If a person makes their goal of advancement clear, their life too becomes clear. The goal of humanity lies in achieving human completion with the cosmic great spirit as the source. In ancient times, humanity guarded the principles of the cosmos, followed them, and both spiritually and physically was just as God's divine will.

Today's humanity respects only human knowledge and does not draw upon the truth of the cosmos. The great way of truth has already fallen into disuse; there is no path for humanity, and in the place where there is no path, people are making a path with human knowledge. As a result of losing their way, the world has become a world of conflict, and people are suffering.

When human thought deteriorates, it brings spiritual deterioration even to the cyclical workings of heaven. Going against the cosmic atmosphere creates irregular climate, causing trouble not only for humanity but for all creation. If things continue as they are, the danger approaches that humanity will kill itself and self-destruct. Science, philosophy, medicine, political science, economics — all must have the spiritual as their base, and the way of things is for the spiritual to manifest and for the physical to be active. Not killing a single thing, not destroying anything, renewing everything, successively manifesting the power of science in new forms, and also renewing physical learning so that it serves human life — this transformation is necessary. Generating new things through the spiritual power from the divine realm, nurturing all things, planning the circulation of life for all the people of the world so that the people of the earth may flourish — this must be woven into the fabric of daily life.

(To be continued)

===4===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt 4

(Continued from last time)

The knowledge of an individual human being, no matter how great a scholar, is so-called "acquired wisdom" and is not the teaching of the laws of the cosmos. Academic learning in the human realm is narrow in scope — it only dissects, analyzes, criticizes, and destroys. With humanism based on this knowledge as its foundation, it can only be said that human completion is a distant prospect. Today's world is one where people study things and instill in themselves a humanitarian spirit through knowledge, believing that truth lies in the world of human knowledge, and merely constructing cosmic truth from human knowledge.

Knowledge is necessary for humanity, but making knowledge the principal thing leads to individualism. Individualism breeds conflict, fans competitive desire for material things, creates competitive desire for honor, and produces conflict at every turn. Because each insists separately and neither yields to the other, the world has become one of division. To align one's spiritual stride, there is no way but to guide and advance by means of cosmic great education. Without understanding cosmic truth, one ends up on a one-sided, narrow, dead-end path. One must link the teaching of the physical side with the spiritual, combining the spiritual and physical, and live human life based on cosmic truth. To live in this world by human knowledge means to seize the world of God and to oppose it. Not walking the path of truth, advancing through actions contrary to divine will, even when one hears words, they become words contrary to natural divine will. For this reason, a heart contrary to divine will arises, sins against heaven accumulate, and there is no shame at all. When one makes a spiritual mistake, since this world is the reflected image of the spirit world, it gives rise to even greater mistakes on the physical side. A person who has not cultivated spiritual refinement may rightly be called blind in the heart. If one knows the spirit world, one understands the truth that the spiritual must be primary, and that the cosmic great spirit is the divine activity of God.

(To be continued)

===5===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt 5

(Published July 1965) "The Dignity of the Human Being"

Who, one may wonder, created this body with its wondrous workings? Scientists see the origin of humanity in the evolution of microorganisms, but while human beings are small life-forms born through the power of great nature, they also constitute a small cosmos. At present 3.2 billion people exist on earth, and not a single face is the same — 3.1 billion (at the time) people each have a different appearance. This is by the great art of nature. It can only be called the mystery of the power of transformation granted to the life of humanity by great nature. In this single physical body, just as in others, one perceives the distribution of life granted equally to all. Furthermore, within the physical body one perceives the flow of great nature's divine will — the great cosmic spirit. Those who perceive this mysterious truth are fortunate. From this precious truth one deeply feels the dignity of the human being. No matter how eloquently one explains the original nature and fundamental essence of humanity, if one cannot feel this precious truth, it is meaningless. Human life is not merely the life of the form visible to the eyes; it is life as a distribution of the great life-force.

===6===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑥

(Published July 1965) "The Sacred Order of All Creation's Formation"

In the formation of all creation, there is a sacred order. The universe, without a single deviation from orbit, lives and acts in perfect orderly sequence. Its appearance is supremely majestic. The fact that all things are produced in proper order is proof that God's strictness manifests in all creation. Strictness, put another way, means following God's divine will. It has been said from ancient times: a gourd vine does not produce an eggplant. Eggplant is eggplant, gourd is gourd, cattle are cattle, horses are horses, dogs are dogs — in proper orderly sequence, based on the nature assigned to each, making that nature clear, and following the cosmic atmosphere and God's divine will, creation continues to be generated.

Whether observing the animal kingdom in terms of truth or in terms of human knowledge, if one awakens to the fact that all things thus strictly follow God's divine will, one cannot but reach the conclusion that this world is truly the world of God.

Fruit trees, vegetables, grains — those that ripen in spring, those that ripen in summer, those that ripen in autumn, those that ripen in winter — all are varied, yet each obediently fulfills its divine mandate, receives the gift of heaven, and properly ripens in the appointed season.

All things honor their season, fulfill the appointment of sun, moon, and time, and fulfill their mission. There is not a single flower that looks at the beauty of another flower and wishes to become like it. The order of nature cannot be broken.

===7===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑦

(Published July 1965) "The Great Way of Divine Nature"

The state of the emergence of all creation, the cycle of the four seasons — if one spiritually observes this, one comes to know that it is the manifestation of God's divine will. Though it is a world of all creation that cannot speak, observing it, one can sense that all creation is crying out with a great voice: "Order is inviolable!" — praising and glorifying the divine will of the cosmic God. If one expresses it this way, the intellectual person will burst out laughing, but to me that voice is audible. When the time comes, all creation rises together with the same momentum — blooming flowers, ripening fruit, joyfully and vigorously active. All creation cannot speak, yet cries out through action. For this reason, the formation of all creation is utterly majestic. There is not a single thing going against the divine will. How, by comparison, does humanity stand? Humanity is praised as the lord of all creation, and is granted in its five-foot body the spiritual power to swallow the great celestial sphere whole, and endowed with intelligence — and yet makes no effort to understand God's divine will, treats its heavenly mission as if it were a dream, and produces nothing but things contrary to divine will. It has forgotten to walk the spiritual path.

I cry out with a loud voice: "Advance along the great way of divine nature!" The great way of divine nature is nothing other than spiritually advancing along the path of God's divine will. There is no choice but for humanity to return to the great way of divine nature and follow the world of God. This is not at all a difficult thing. The first step is to return to and become naturalized in the ancestral God (Mioya) who created us, and to cultivate the spirit of becoming completely divine. As soon as possible, one must resolutely carry out the renewal and restoration of one's own spirit. The world will no longer be the world of humans but will become the world of God, and people too will become divine. Purifying this world as the world of God, the spirits of past ancestors will be saved, we who are present will be saved, and future descendants will also be saved and flourish. Spirit will naturally manifest in action, the universe will flourish, and humanity will be perfected.

===9===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑨

(Published July 1965) "In Accordance with God's Divine Will"

God has created a world of affection in which the people of the world live in harmony and love. This is God's divine plan. Resenting others, envying others, a narrow heart — these are contrary to God's divine will. All creation on earth is born from God's divine will, and so this world is the world of God. Since we dwell in this wondrous divine world, we as human beings must master God's divine will, revere all creation without treating anything carelessly, handle everything with care, live our lives in gratitude for all things in heaven, earth, and the cosmos. God's divine will illuminates the earth, loves all creation, and extends divine protection. Only by knowing this precious truth does one truly become a person. By the power of all things in heaven and earth, one can brightly greet each day. Beginning with humanity, all creation is born in diverse ways; fulfilling one's calling according to one's divine mandate is one's mission. By fulfilling one's mission, boarding the spirit of unity of all creation in the cosmos as one, one can spend an incomparably happy life. Today, through the power of intellectual persons, people walk the path of man-made morality and devote themselves to strengthening intellectual morality. As quickly as possible, taking the power of heaven as a mirror and receiving the spirit of all creation in the cosmos into one's heart as soon as possible, one must be renewed.

===10===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑩

(Published July 1965) "Humanity is the Lord of All Creation"

Humanity is the lord (reichō) of all creation. "Lord of all creation" means to lead through spirit. The character for "lead" (chō / 長) carries meanings of: long, far, great, good, constant, noble and exalted, the head, to nurture, to guide, to teach, and so on. The activity of spirit can know the great activity of the universe. "To lead" (nagamaru) means to continue the activity of spirit long and eternally without end. This is called the mission of heaven. To understand the activity of spirit and nourish the heart with that power is the true path of humanity and is the most important path.

If one considers why humanity is the lord of all creation, one must know the essence and character of spirit. When "all creation" is spoken of, it refers to the spirit bestowed upon all created things — birds, beasts, grasses, trees, and everything. The scope of all spirits is vast; viewed with spiritual eyes, all things are bestowed with spirit, and the cosmos is filled with spirit until there is no place left to step. Humanity, the lord of all creation, stands in a yin-yang relationship with all creation; the path is for all creation and humanity together to perform the workings of the cosmos. If humanity infuses the spirit bestowed upon all creation with the power of love, and on earth devises the way of creation and nurturing, then all creation too returns virtue to humanity. This is a repayment of grace in a physical and material way.

===11===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑪

(Published July 1965) "Welcoming God into the Heart"

All creation does not possess the power to expand its active force in all directions following God's divine will. Only humanity, as the lord of all creation, can discern the ancestral will of God. Grateful for and moved by this profound divine blessing, one should become the soul of the universe and be active. To everyone, God has given the truth of the natural universe in an easily understandable way. A person who discerns the cosmic divine will and acts naturally comes to embody the authority of God, and can understand that in divine-human union one is together with God.

Knowing the divine nature, one knows human nature. Human nature is given by God; spiritually, mastering the divine nature and making human nature clear is called faith. One who does not know the divine nature consequently cannot understand human nature either. God cannot be understood through explanation, for God is not something that can be explained. Humanity has no choice but to sincerely and wholeheartedly hear the truth of the cosmos and welcome God into one's own heart.

===12===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑫

(Published July 1965)

"The Awakening of Humanity"

If the heart becomes clear through the teachings of the way, a person leaves the world of conflict and comes to live in the spiritual world. Working spiritually, all creation lives along with it. Since this world is the world of God, when the divine power of nature fills and overflows, all things are revived. For this reason, if the spiritual gem of humanity does not awaken, there is nothing left to say about the present world but "all is at an end."

Originally, humanity was born into the world especially as the lord of all creation and as a beloved child of God; taught the way of use and enrichment in the likeness of the God of creation and nurturing; and granted free will in order to open heaven and earth without limit. This is the original way of being for humanity. Abusing and misusing that free will, indulging in self-interest and self-seeking, drowning in self-love, hating others, becoming angry, envious, resentful, and fighting with strong bitterness — unless one changes direction, awakens to cosmic truth, and advances on the path of life just as the divine will of great nature, a terrible situation will arise. Looking at the state of the world: boasting of having conquered great nature, claiming to have opened the door of cosmic mystery — such arrogance and recklessness are extreme. From God's perspective there is nothing to call it but ignorant and foolish, and people are being led toward the mountain of death. It is clearer than fire that if one goes against the principles of heaven and earth, one will eventually stumble and fall.

===13===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑬

(Published July 1965) "Humanity is a Microcosm of the Universe"

The human body is constituted by the power of the divine spirit-elements. And the body is an instrument of the heart. Through the instrument of the feeling heart, it performs the work of spiritually mastering in the heart the spirit of all creation in the cosmos. For this reason, the human body is called a microcosm of the universe. Put another way, humanity, as inheritor of the cosmic great spirit and inheritor of the cosmic original body, is a being of great dignity. Through the bond of God's great spirit and humanity's small spirit, there is a minute working in the minutest, invisible places. The human body was created by God perfectly and without flaw. For this reason, a person is also divine. If one awakens to this truth, one can spiritually master the cosmos in this five-foot body — this is expressed as "swallowing the cosmos whole."

The self-awareness that a person is themselves divine is developed through practice. Through practice one is granted the power to penetrate the ancestral God of the heart and to discern all creation of the cosmos. And furthermore, this world itself, just as it is, is the world of God. Yet despite being the world of God, people do not seek the ancestral God of the heart spiritually; without spiritual foundation, they measure things by the physical learning of individual knowledge and advance through knowledge — which is the height of regret. As a result of insufficient spiritual working, people fall day by day into a pitiful state of humans who spend their time in petty conflicts of self-interest. To make this world the original world of God, there is no other way than to grant humanity the truth of the cosmos — that is, the power of God. Through this, the world will become exactly as God's divine will, people will walk the righteous path, naturally a world of peace will come, and they will be able to walk the path of happiness. If one walks the path of God, one will not fall into evil ways or superstition; and if one illuminates all creation by the path of truth, there is no need for argument or theory — a clear and pure world will visit. Religion is what teaches the spiritual path in order to understand the divine will of the cosmic God.

===14===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑭

(Published July 1965) "Knowing Cosmic Life through the Heart"

If one understands the divine life of the great natural universe, heaven will naturally cause one to realize it. Since humanity is a child of the cosmic God, knowing the world of divine spirit is humanity's path. However, please know that what one sees from the spirit world differs in nature from things in the present world. The way of seeing is also spiritual, and there is neither name nor good and evil. Here one must consider that humanity has given names to all things in heaven, earth, and creation. By this, life was given to all creation, the activity of all creation became clear, and all creation became effective.

At the beginning of the world, sound was the beginning, and it was through sound that creation was made. That is, sound is the divine spirit-element, and through the activity of sound all creation was constituted. By this principle, ears are necessary for human beings. The ear is an instrument of the heart; even the discernment of words through sound is not discerned by the ear itself — it is the heart that discerns all things. The heart has that power. Eyes, mouth, and nose too are given in order to know cosmic life. And all of them are instruments of the heart. It is an eye that sees spiritually, a nose that smells spiritually, a mouth that tastes spiritually. Although it is said that the eyes see things, the power is not the eyes seeing things. It is the heart that discerns all things and spiritually discerns with the heart. The nose too does not smell with the nose itself. Both physically and spiritually it is the power of the heart that smells and discerns. The mouth likewise.

===15===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑮

(Published July 1965)

"The Way of Faith"

The duty of humanity lies in advancing on the way of faith and purifying the spirit. Faith guards the life of humanity, draws upon the feelings of affection in all things, and enables harmonious and loving mutual life. A person who guards God's divine will becomes rich in heart; spiritually creates a peaceful world, advances along the path of flourishing. The cosmic God desires this life of joy for humanity; the daily joy of advancing life is the bond of divine-human union. Religion must teach and guide and realize this unity of God and humanity. To reveal to the human world every aspect of the cosmic divine will is called divine mystery. With divine mystery, the path of rightly guarding the laws of the cosmos becomes clear.

God guides the life of all existence through divine revelation. God is boundless and vast, the supreme authority. Making that state clear, strictly and with great love and warmth, God advances along the path for humanity. To transfer this divine mandate to humanity and fulfill that mission is the duty of the person. Accordingly, faith is the truth that polishes the spirit-soul which is humanity's original nature — both outwardly and inwardly — by the divine power of natural God, enables people to live harmoniously with one another, to understand the teachings of the great life-force, and to guide life toward longevity. Know that this is the true law and the way of humanity.

===16===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑯

(Published July 1965)

"Humans are Nurtured by the Way and Bear the Nature of Earth"

All creation is nurtured by the three bloods of the sun, moon, and great earth; these three, the "three manifestations," are called the Way. The totality of heaven, earth, and all creation is the universe; one must be aware that we are people who receive the vital essence of the blood of sun, moon, and earth. Humanity is called the spiritual gem of the universe. Put another way, this means that humanity receives the profound virtue of the divine spirit. For this reason, the ideal is to understand the cosmic great spirit, and to become a person of divine-human union who comprehends God's divine activity. Only in divine-human union does a person have the qualification to be called the lord of all creation. The heavenly mission grants to humanity the power to live following the divine will of the cosmic great ancestral God. A person must understand this heavenly mission and strive to live attaining the highest virtue.

With the earth as the principal body and the power of sun and moon, all creation is nurtured. Even a single blade of grass sprouts from and grows through the earth; the power of growth is illuminated by the sun, and moisture is regulated by the moon. One must also be aware that humanity is born having received the nature of the earth. Hair is grasses and trees; skin is the ground; blood vessels are rivers; nerves are roads. Teeth and bones are rocks; the body corresponds to land. There are places in the body that can be likened to rice paddies and fields. This is because humanity bears the nature of the earth.

Races differ because in each country people receive the blood (earth) of that country's land, and people born accustomed to that land differ in constitution and so on. Children resemble their parents at birth because they receive the blood of their parents. People differ by race because they receive the blood of the great earth. Earth is blood, and blood is spirit. The spiritual ancestral God of the land is called in our country the Ubusuna deity. It is the working that produced the earth of that town or village; the spirit that became earth; and also the working and power — the blood — of the earth that blesses all the townspeople and villagers with food, clothing, and shelter; this profound virtue is revered as divine and called the Ubusuna deity. "Ubu" (産) means to bind, and to bind means to unite God and humanity. The basis of Ubusuna is reverence and God. The bond is the soul (tamashii), and when a person is born, the soul is granted by the Ubusuna deity. Because a person is born bound to God, they are born in the form accustomed to that land.

===17===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑰

(Published July 1965)

"When Humanity Advances, All Creation Flourishes"

If a person advances in accordance with the divine will of the heavenly mandate, this results in the nourishment of the heart, and one advances spiritually. Mysteriously, as the spirit becomes vast, the body too grows larger. If humanity returns to and assimilates into the great spirit and conforms to the cosmic will, the great earth also grows larger. That the great earth grows larger means that the power of the earth increases. If the power of the earth increases and the land becomes fertile, there will be no more barren land — that is, the surface area of arable land expands. There will be no more need to fight over land. The history of bloodshed in conflicts over colonies is a record of human ignorance and faithlessness. If humanity returns to and assimilates into the great spirit and follows the cosmic will, both the earth and humanity will be given spiritual power and will grow larger. When human spirit advances, all people and creation will flourish more abundantly than ever, and conflicts over land and the food crisis will be resolved. If the hearts of farmers become pure, the five grains can sing of bountiful harvest, and fruit will grow larger and more flavorful. Put another way, along with the advancement of the spiritual gem of humanity, all people and creation advance, and ultimately the earth itself, and all grasses and trees, will all flourish. This wondrous principle cannot be explained by science. It is a great error to think that fertilizer alone will bring a harvest. When the world becomes a battleground and human conflict intensifies, the evil spirit of conflict fills the air, exhaling evil breath; since that ugly spirit opposes the cosmic atmosphere, one must know that it has a bad influence on crops as well. Looking up at heaven in gratitude for sun and moon, bowing to the earth in gratitude for its grace, coming into contact with the cosmic atmosphere in reverence and humility — if one cultivates with this spirit, crops will naturally grow lush and green and bear abundant fruit. The ideal climate of "five winds and ten rains" is also not bestowed unless the human world becomes righteous; and if not, it leads to the bringing of three calamities and five disasters — the harm of wind, water, and fire.

===18===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑱

(Published July 1965) "Living According to the Truth of the Universe"

Truly and mysteriously, when humanity — the spirit-soul of the universe — becomes perfect, the universe too grows even larger. When human spirit advances, the universe too flourishes. If one awakens to this wondrous bond, one will realize that the path of flourishing for both the cosmic universe and humanity is not merely the individual renewal of spirit, but making the earth a place where all of humanity lives as one body under the cosmic great life-force. It is the heavenly mandate and the way of life humanity must guard that all of humanity lives exactly as God's divine will. Knowing this heavenly grace, the foundation is to extend that virtue to all people and creation and to pray to God for the flourishing of the universe. If one understands the happiness of the person who lives receiving the profound virtue of sun, moon, and earth, one cannot but become righteous and pure. A person is divine, and a child of God. God and we cannot be separated. Heaven and earth cannot be separated. Heaven, earth, and all creation cannot be separated. Upon the total unity view, all advance and flourish. Only with the earth does the sun become clear; only with the sun does the earth become clear; heaven and earth together combine their power, and all creation on earth is constituted. For this reason, to live exactly as God's divine will is the divine mandate of the heart, and faith is to know the true nature of the cosmos, to live in gratitude for all creation following the heavenly mandate, and to be thoroughly devoted to a life lived according to the truth of the universe.

===19===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑲

(Published July 1965)

"The Way of Happiness"

Humanity's purpose is to know what happiness is and to know the path to happiness. It lies in realizing that there is a great teaching that transforms, through the divine way, the misfortune created by human knowledge into happiness; in feeling gratitude for having access to this great teaching; and in holding the resolve to put this great teaching into practice.

Human life was once described as fifty years — a short life — but today the average male lifespan is sixty-five years and the female lifespan seventy-two (as of the July 1965 publication), and as the age of spiritual civilization arrives, lifespan will grow longer. The body may have its cycles of rise and fall, but the spirit knows no aging and does not decline. The reason that people of faith maintain long life is by this principle. The spirit of the faithful, even after death, lives in the true spirit realm (shadow realm) close to God. Death is an inescapable destiny in human life, but death is not at all something to grieve. The body is the vessel of the spirit and the vessel of life — the place of cultivation and practice of one's spirit-soul. The spirit lives in the great eternal life-force. The spiritual life lived in this spirit is the secret of happiness in human life. This happiness cannot be obtained except by knowing the way of the cosmos. The way is life, truth, and the source of happiness. If one yields the self and rightly turns the direction of the heart, God will teach the way through one's surroundings — not to the point of being a spiritual sage, but even so. Whether through the words of a person, or in the various phenomena that enter the eyes, God reveals the divine will. Without neglecting the practice of receiving this, advancing spiritually, the spirit is strengthened; one gains intuition, partakes of great virtue, and can receive great benefit. Even a tree, even an insect, even a single flower — all are telling something to a person. If one removes what clings to the heart and quietly observes, one can receive something from them. To come into contact with the mystery of great nature and to have the attitude of probing deep into all things — this is the practice that reaches the state of divine-human oneness. In that practice, one can taste an unsurpassed sense of happiness.

===20===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ⑳

(Published July 1965)

"Great Nature as Teacher"

Plants are governed by the power of natural heaven, growing just as God's divine will through the power of creation and nurturing; since they do not possess the five emotions, they grow purely under God's loving grace. That they lack the five emotions is by God's loving grace — for the sake of the tree that does not have the freedom to move itself in case of fire, they are not given the suffering of feeling hot; when cut, they are not given the pain of feeling hurt. Thus the need for humanity's care of plants arises, and when plants receive human care they grow lush and flourishing. As if in exchange, or as gratitude, plants all work actively for humanity. For example, rapeseed ripens its seeds and provides oil, giving humanity public benefit. Trees have virtue and, acting exactly as God's divine will in the cosmos, give great bliss to humanity. Without timber, houses cannot be built, and there would be a lack of fuel. Humanity should be grateful to plants and devote itself to their flourishing — this is the heaven-given affection and mission of the lord of all creation. Trees also have truly mysterious workings, calling up the wind and living together with the wind. Is not humanity revived by the cool breeze of the tree? Trees, when cut and used, become fire, become earth, and act to nurture trees once more. The will of the tree is as nature itself. It grows in the natural world. Humanity too, observing the form of the tree and taking it as a mirror, making a life that follows great nature — this is obtaining nature as one's teacher. This is why the tree is regarded as king; take the tree as the center of plants, and treat it as the object through which to obtain the highest virtue. However, one must not judge by the appearance of the tree and cut its spirit. For the tree reveals in color each of the four seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, and makes things known through form.

A person who has no gratitude for plants is opposing the divine will of the cosmic God.

===21===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ㉑

(Published July 1965)

"Streamers and Carp Banners"

For a long time I have been filled with deep admiration for the many beautiful customs reflecting religious spirit — customs in which the ancestors of the Japanese people, who have lived according to the divine way since ancient times, have understood the laws of nature and the principles of nature and given them life in their everyday lives and customs.

In May, in households with male children, five-colored streamers and carp banners have been raised to celebrate the fifth-month festival. No one knows who first began this, but its meaning is deep.

In spring all creation sprouts, and mountain and field are filled with a vivid green landscape. Tree branches put forth flowers, and grasses open flowers at their crowns — it is said to be "a thousand purples and ten thousand crimsons," adorned in five colors. It is the great sky that gives these five colors. The rays of the sun go from yellow through green; the sky is blue; the red sun rises from the east and at midday becomes pure white; at evening the process reverses and the sky becomes dark. The great sky is a body active in five colors. Taking these five colors as a model, the ancient Japanese erected five-colored banners and used them as the colors of the streamers. The five colors are given to all creation from the great sky according to the principles of the sky. Flowing down from the great sky, these five colors are carried to earth and give color and flavor to everything, including plants, promoting growth. When streamers are erected, the colors become even stronger in the surrounding area, and the streamers serve as an intermediary and relay station for drawing in the colors of the great sky. The streamer is a symbol of the simple faith of praying to heaven for the growth of the infant. This sentiment reaches heaven, and the profound virtue of the streamer, though invisible to the eye, is a ceremony of deep and meaningful virtue. In Japan it is felt to be a celebration among celebrations. In spring, when the season becomes full of vital energy, if one puts one's ear to a cedar tree, one can hear the sound of water being drawn up from between the wood and bark to the branches. The carp banner is what I observed from the spirit world as a symbol of this vital, energetic activity of all creation drawing up water in spring. As the saying goes, "carp climbing a waterfall" — in spring, all creation draws up water in vigorous activity that presents the appearance of a waterfall. The carp banner is the form in which the appearance of an infant growing up vigorously and swiftly, like climbing a waterfall, is embodied and prayed for. Since it is a representation of nature, it has become a children's celebration; its meaning is also deep: raising banners with the truth of the five colors, and praying for growth by receiving the spirited heart of the carp and the spirit of the great sky — this is the expression of the sincere devotion of the people of God. Both streamers and carp banners are not physical things but spiritual things expressed in physical form, made into celebration and festival. The Hinamatsuri (Doll Festival) of the third day of the third month for female children is a festival event of the same significance.

===22===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ㉒

(Published July 1965) "The Three Great Celebrations of Life (1)"

The three great celebrations of life should be birth, marriage, and ascension to heaven. The auspiciousness of birth and marriage is a festive occasion everyone acknowledges without question, but it would be difficult to understand making ascension to heaven a day of celebration. One does not set up this paradox — calling this death, which the people of the world regard as life's greatest sorrow, life's greatest celebration — to revel in novelty.

Life and death in human life are an inevitable providence arising from the orderly rhythm of all creation's generation and nurturing. Since humanity is the lord of all creation, by the providence of the divine way, after death one returns to the spirit realm (shadow realm) and comes to live one's life in the spirit world. The physical body presently on earth is merely the body used during that preparatory period; the true self is the spirit. This is the reason for regarding ascension to heaven as the greatest auspicious event in human life.

(Excerpt omitted)

Human life is originally such that one's true home is the spirit world, and that the heart, using the body called the physical body as a temporary vessel, appears in the present world for spiritual practice, and then departs once more for one's true homeland — the gateway called death is the setting forth for that journey. Physical relatives will grieve on the bodily side, but conversely, the spiritual parents in the spirit world rejoice, welcoming the newborn, and also rejoice at welcoming one who has accomplished great things and achieved great fame — this is the God and parent of the spirit world. Therefore, religion, in its true nature, must thoroughly teach the reality of the spirit world, its true nature and levels, life in the spirit world, and so on — giving people in the present world firm conviction and peace of mind regarding the inevitable eternal dwelling place they must return to, and thoroughly devoting itself to the true teachings that enable return to the spirit world (shadow realm). "The frog in the well does not know the great ocean" — this is the behavior of modern humanity. Sufficiently receiving the blessing of the cosmic great ancestral God as spiritual nourishment in one's lifetime, mastering the way of the spiritual person, exerting oneself in one's work, without attachment, without anxiety for the future, having completely fulfilled one's mission as a human being — with the spirited heart of a graduating student, amid the tears of rejoicing family, one must make it a great celebratory day.

===23===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ㉓

(Published July 1965) "The Three Great Celebrations of Life (2)"

Grasses that seem to sprout in spring and already wither by summer; small animals like the humble mayfly that are born in the morning and die in the evening — yet as long as there is life, there is not a single living thing among all plants and animals that does not leave behind seeds and descendants for future generations. The fact that all living and plant things continue to exist into the eternal future by repeating the cycle of life and death is a divine work of eternal life granted by God. The matter of life and death, from the perspective of God who presides over the cosmos, is no different whether looking back one hundred thousand years or at the present or forward hundreds of millions of years into the future. Insects become larvae, then butterflies, then moths, then eggs in the branches of trees, according to the season. The egg is the beginning of the insect and also the end. Are the first egg and the last egg truly the same thing? After all, this is merely a kind of transformation. Human beings too pass through childhood, youth, young adulthood, middle age, and old age, and return to the form of death — which is, in essence, merely a process of transformation in the course of life that continues without ceasing into the eternal future and does not perish. This body is the flesh transmitted from ancestors, created by God. All creation in the cosmos, since God created it, has been identical for hundreds of millions and hundreds of millions of years, and will not change in the slightest for the eternal future. That which does not perish in the process of eternal time does not become fixed and change. Humanity should receive life and death as the most auspicious things occurring within the advancing divine work of all creation's generation and nurturing.

===24===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt 24

(Published July 1965)

The Purpose of Life and the Mission of Humanity

The purpose of human life is not merely to taste happiness and pleasure in the present world. Yet the great majority of people cling to happiness and pleasure alone, are anxious to escape from suffering and disaster, and fall entirely into petty, self-centered love. The mission for which God created humanity in this world cannot be something so shallow as to cause them to indulge in ease. Humanity is endowed with the unlimited power of God and granted spiritual nature and spiritual wisdom — that is, at all times one has the nature to refine these and reach the state of God. Understanding well God's divine purpose and divine plan, accumulating virtue anew day by day, living a righteous life, becoming aware of being an angel called to work for the heavenly and earthly great plan of bringing about world peace — with this awareness, one must devote oneself body and soul and be actively and vigorously engaged. Here lies the dignity of the sacred law of quieting the material and self-centered soul, returning to the world of the cosmic great spirit realm, and returning to God — the method of soul-settling and returning to God — and through this spiritual law, advancing to the state of divine-human union, it is concretely demonstrated that humanity, through communion with the spirit world, can reach the realm of God. Moreover, this is the most correct and most straightforward practice method.

===25===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt

㉕

(Published July 1965) "The Spiritual Power of the Universe's One Spring"

A person who understands the life of the human world, the life of the earth, and the life of the universe is said to be a person with great magnanimity. If one knows heaven and knows the earth, no matter what happens or occurs, one will not be thrown into confusion.

In the spiritual world, the way is to follow the law with heaven and earth as the standard. There is a phrase for measuring a person: great magnanimity or small magnanimity. Magnanimity refers to the spiritual capacity of a person's heart. Great magnanimity is nothing other than knowing and measuring the world. To raise the magnanimity to know and measure the world, and to know and measure the universe, is the ultimate. Though humanity has a five-foot body, spiritually one has the magnanimity to swallow the universe in one spring. God has granted humanity the power to do freely anything with words. If one communes with God, anything — even affairs of all under heaven — can be known in the present world. Knowing the truth of the cosmos, one can know oneself. No matter how much one prays for individual completion, it is impossible by human power. If one draws the cosmic great spirit into the heart according to its principles, one can know the teachings of the cosmos, and if one's own mistakes become clear, the divine will of the natural God of the cosmos becomes well understood. To understand, one first makes it clear in words. Being grateful to the cosmos, being grateful for words, humbly creating a world of life exactly as God's divine will — thereby a person instantly communes with God. With only the attitude of one's heart toward the mystery of the cosmos, one can fly into the divine realm.

===26===
From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ㉖

(Published July 1965) "One Spirit, Four Souls"

Knowledge is physical; the spiritual refers to the true, formless heart. Humanity, as the lord of all creation, must work with both these sides.

If the workings of the four souls are complete in a person, a spiritual working arises that accords with God's divine will; but people with all four souls fully functioning are rare. Depending on the person, only one soul may be working. "One soul" refers to the case where one measures everything with individual wisdom, without ethics or human feeling, working by knowledge alone. Or there are those with only one soul outstanding — a rough warrior-like person, or a person who is a bundle of gentleness, a person who is one-sided. The four souls — ara (rough), nigi (harmonious), sachi (fortunate), and kushi (wondrous) — their four characteristic workings unified as one is called spirit; from ancient times this has been called "one spirit, four souls." When a person dies, instead of calling the soul "reikon" (spirit-soul), it is sometimes called "konpaku." When a person ends with only a soul, and the soul is purified in the spirit world, this is called konpaku. When one understands God while still alive, the spirit settles into the person's physical body, so it is called reikon. Since the human heart is a derived portion of the great spirit, a person is granted from birth the power to seek spirit. If one seeks the divine spirit, the reikon is bestowed in accordance. To express this heavenly mandate is spiritual activity.

Humanity, as the lord of all creation, possesses wondrous and inexplicable power, is endowed with divine wisdom, and is given the power to probe to the ultimate, able to enter the world of sensation and obtain the highest intuition. The source from which humanity obtains the highest intuition is in the great void. For this reason, one must strive to receive spiritual power from the great void. If one completes the four souls commanded by God, sensitive spiritual workings arise through faith in God. There is nothing at all in the affairs of the cosmos and all creation that one cannot know. If one proceeds pursuing the best in the human world and communing with the great spirit of the cosmos, the great spirit too advances, and together the spirit of humanity advances, and both heart and matter develop. This is the human mission commanded by God.

===27===
:27
:From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ㉗
:(Published July 1965)
:"Divine Nature and Human Heart-Nature"

:Humanity, the lord of all creation, is the most exalted and contains a rich divine nature. The heart-nature of humanity has an instinct to return to the divine nature of the cosmos. That which is created inherently harbors an appropriate divine nature, and always has a centripetal force seeking to return to its origin. That all creation yearns for and adores humanity — which as the ideal being is nearest to God — and takes it as its aspiration to imitate humanity even a little, is the manifestation of this centripetal force.

:When a person is born into this world, the heart-nature is originally linked to the divine spirit; it is connected to a spirit-thread called tama-no-o (the thread of the gem), which was distributed and descended from the great spirit of the cosmos through a thousand separations. The physical body is constituted from the chromosomes of the father's and mother's cells through heredity, and is nourished from the mother's body through the umbilical cord, forming and shaping the body to be born. If one deeply studies the heart-nature and physical organization of humanity, one can understand the true nature of the cosmos.

:The great earth is the first of all creation, its flower, its fruit, and its crystal. Among all creation generated and nurtured on that earth, humanity is its framework and the highest existence. The power of creation and transformation always renews itself without ceasing, and the working of the divine atmosphere creates all things infinitely. This is centrifugal force. On the bodily side, one separates into infinite varieties and grows distant from God; but in contrast, on the side of the heart, there is a centripetal activity seeking to return to God, to God. God, among all created things, purposed the creation of humanity so that the perfect image of the self could be reflected; a person is a small cosmos that has received the cosmos intact within oneself. A person is called a child of God, and has received divine nature — to a degree immeasurably many times greater than anything else.

===29===
:29
:From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ㉙
:(Published July 1965)
:"Live with Spirit as Master, Body as Servant"

:The physical body is the form of the heart. It is the direct manifestation of the heart, and corresponds to the heart. What constitutes the principal body of the physical body is blood. The entire body has blood as its source. Blood nourishes and sustains the tissue cells throughout the entire body. Blood must constantly be purified and replenished. What drives this is the action of respiration; through breathing, blood is constantly purified, receives the nourishment of air, circulates through the entire body and sustains it. This blood is the true nature of the heart — the divine nature given by God. Receiving new nourishment through the action of respiration is receiving the light of God through the tama-no-o (spirit thread).

:That blood spiritualizes to form the spiritual body; that which governs the respiratory system is the direct nerves, and that which governs the circulatory system is the sympathetic nerves; that the brain — the center of the nerves — corresponds to the supreme celestial sphere where God dwells, and that the torso, which contains the digestive system and others, corresponds to the earth — if these are examined against the true nature of the cosmos, the structure and function of the human body are truly mysterious, and their significance is deep.

:The ancestral origin of spirit is the celestial sphere, and the ancestral origin of the body is the earth. For this reason, the order is established that spirit is the root and body is the branch, and it goes without saying that the heart should be placed above the body. Strictly speaking, since both spirit and body are given by God, there should be no above or below; but in terms of the sequence in which influence is exerted, spirit becomes the root and body becomes the branch. To use the heart for the benefit of the body is clearly "body-primary, spirit-secondary" — that it is going against the cosmic fundamental principle and order is perfectly clear. Originally there is neither good nor evil; just as the divine way, just as God's divine will, is the natural way of being. To do "body-primary, spirit-secondary" is called evil. The degree to which one goes against the divine atmosphere is the degree of evil; corresponding to it, "spirit-primary, body-secondary" is what is called the degree of good.

:Mistakenly believing that the way of body-primary, spirit-secondary is the truth, thinking it natural that the superior prevail over the inferior for self-preservation, taking the strong-eating-the-weak principle as one's attitude in life, and believing in this as a superstition — it is because of this that falsehood is generated in the world. Since evil and falsehood are inherently impermissible, one creates hell by one's own hand. In contrast, the way of spirit-primary, body-secondary takes as truth the natural way of being that seeks to approach and return to God.

===30===
:30
:From "The Joy of Human Completion," excerpt ㉚
:(Published July 1965)
:"The Way of Reason in Heaven, Earth, and Nature"

:The divine will of God may well be called the love of great nature. What bursts forth from the substance of that love as the divine power of creation and transformation is divine wisdom. Divine wisdom is, so to speak, the means of creation and transformation. One can nod in understanding even from observing the sun. The sun itself is a mass of heat, but when it extends its power to the earth, it comes running as light and stops on the earth. In the places touched by that light, it leaves a corresponding heat. This heat is life. God gives light to all creation, transforms by divine wisdom, and in the places where that light stops, plants an aspect of the self — the actual substance that is love. And the created things are each given an appropriate divine nature. Looking at the form of plants growing by the heat that the sun's light brings — one can understand this principle. Humanity is given divine nature from God through the tama-no-o corresponding to the sun's light. For this reason, the essence of the human heart is love. The means by which that love acts toward others — that is, it acts as wisdom. By receiving through the tama-no-o the unceasing divine wisdom — divine will — humanity maintains life and nourishes the essence of the heart.

:No matter how lofty the spirit received from God, if one's own heart does not understand it, it does not enter the heart. Since it does not dissolve into the substance of the heart that governs one's own life, it is immediately lost — that is, it only remains in the world of knowledge which is the surface of the heart. A person, following the principle of spirit-primary, body-secondary, mastering the manifestation of the life of great nature in the celestial astronomy of the heavenly body, receives cosmic great education and also receives light, dissolves it into the substance of the heart, digests it, and can rightly nourish and advance the heart. Once this is reversed to body-primary, spirit-secondary, and the heart becomes a servant of the physical body, one instead takes in falsehood from the knowledge hell and accumulates evil. Today's people have almost entirely fallen into body-primary, spirit-secondary. Are they not loving those who have loved them while turning their backs on God? They are going against the heavenly and earthly natural principle of loving God, loving others, and loving the way. The further a person advances by the working of knowledge, the further they fall into hell. In the end, there is no way out but the complete destruction of the entire world.

:If one makes clear the relationship between divine nature and heart-nature, one will realize the great error of misusing science. While one agrees without reluctance to efforts by intellectuals to develop science and plan the development and progress of products, one cannot but give warning that they do not fall into hell because of science.
